title: Ἀνὴρ μεσοπόλιος καὶ ἑταῖραι
titleEn: The Middle-Aged Man and His Two Mistresses
part: The Middle-Aged Man and His Two Mistresses (Chambry 52 · Perry 31)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 52 (= Perry 31). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἀνὴρ μεσοπόλιος δύο ἐρωμένας εἶχεν, ὧν ἡ μὲν νέα ὑπῆρχεν, ἡ δὲ πρεσβῦτις.
sentences.tr: Anēr mesopolios dyo erōmenas eichen, hōn hē men nea hypērchen, hē de presbytis.
sentences.l: A half-grey man had two mistresses, of whom the one was young, the other elderly.
sentences.i: A man going grey had two mistresses, one young and the other old.
sentences.n: μεσοπόλιος, 'half-grey', is the word for middle age; ἐρωμένη is a woman loved, feminine throughout. ἡ μέν … ἡ δέ divides a pair, 'the one … the other'; μέν … δέ is Greek's constant balancing device and shapes this whole fable, in which the two women are exact mirrors.

sentences.t: Καὶ ἡ μὲν προβεβηκυῖα αἰδουμένη νεωτέρῳ αὐτῆς πλησιάζειν, διετέλει, εἴ ποτε πρὸς αὐτὴν παρεγένετο, τὰς μελαίνας αὐτοῦ τρίχας περιαιρουμένη.
sentences.tr: Kai hē men probebēkuia aidoumenē neōterōi autēs plēsiazein, dietelei, ei pote pros autēn paregeneto, tas melainas autou trichas periairoumenē.
sentences.l: And the advanced-in-years one, ashamed to consort with a man younger than herself, kept on, whenever he came to her, plucking out his black hairs.
sentences.i: The elder, ashamed to be keeping company with a man younger than herself, would pull out his black hairs whenever he came to her.
sentences.n: διετέλει with the participle περιαιρουμένη is the supplementary participle: διατελέω 'continue' takes a participle for the thing continued — 'she kept on plucking'. προβεβηκυῖα, 'having gone forward' (in years), is the courteous word for old.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ νεωτέρα ὑποστελλομένη γέροντα ἐραστὴν ἔχειν τὰς πολιὰς αὐτοῦ ἀπέσπα.
sentences.tr: Hē de neōtera hypostellomenē geronta erastēn echein tas polias autou apespa.
sentences.l: And the younger, shrinking from having an old man as a lover, kept tearing out his grey hairs.
sentences.n: ὑποστελλομένη … ἔχειν, 'drawing back from having': the verb takes an infinitive for the thing shrunk from, just as αἰδουμένη did in the sentence before. ἀπέσπα is imperfect, like διετέλει before it — both women are at it repeatedly. πολιαί, 'the grey ones', with θρίξ left unexpressed.

sentences.t: Οὕτω τε συνέβη αὐτῷ ὑπὸ ἀμφοτέρων ἐν μέρει τιλλομένῳ φαλακρὸν γενέσθαι.
sentences.tr: Houtō te synebē autōi hypo amphoterōn en merei tillomenōi phalakron genesthai.
sentences.l: And so it came about for him, being plucked by both in turn, to become bald.
sentences.i: And so, plucked by both in turn, he ended up bald.
sentences.n: συνέβη with the infinitive, 'it came about that…'; αὐτῷ … τιλλομένῳ are datives agreeing with each other and hanging on συνέβη. ἐν μέρει, 'in turn'.

sentences.t: Οὕτω πανταχοῦ τὸ ἀνώμαλον ἐπιβλαβές ἐστι.
sentences.tr: Houtō pantachou to anōmalon epiblabes esti.
sentences.l: So everywhere what is uneven is harmful.
sentences.i: So it is that anything ill-matched is everywhere a source of harm.
sentences.n: Οὕτω πανταχοῦ, 'so, everywhere' — a closing hinge of the same family as οὕτω καί. τὸ ἀνώμαλον is literally 'the uneven', what does not match; here the mismatch of ages.
